vendor: Tracer Management Systems Limited (trading as Joblogic)
title: Rugged tablet for Joblogic: UK buyer's guide
meta_description: Joblogic publishes Android 7.0 or later with 4GB RAM. The Tuga A10 (Android 14, 8GB RAM, IP68) meets both for job forms, photos and signatures on site.
intro: Joblogic is a field service management system for service contractors, built and sold from the UK by Tracer Management Systems Limited, which trades as Joblogic and gives a Birmingham address on its site. The vendor describes it as connecting jobs, engineers, assets, compliance, quotes and invoices in one system, and lists mechanical and electrical, HVAC and refrigeration, fire and security, facilities management and plumbing and heating among more than 30 trades it covers. The office plans and schedules work in the web product; engineers receive and complete that work in the Joblogic Mobile app.

The mobile app is where the site work happens. The vendor's Google Play listing says engineers capture time sheets, notes, parts, expenses, mileage, photos and signatures, and that bespoke forms can replace risk assessments, gas and electrical certificates, equipment service sheets and customer satisfaction forms. Its user guide documents a Scan option that opens the camera to find assets by QR code or barcode, and its FAQ says the app can be used without signal. That is a device that lives in a van, goes up ladders, into plant rooms and loft spaces, and gets handed to a customer for a signature, which is where a consumer tablet with a glass back and no sealing tends to fail early.

This page sets out what Joblogic publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published requirements, where the Windows option fits and where it does not, and how a UK contractor can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet.

requirements.requirement: Android 7.0 or later with a minimum of 4GB RAM
requirements.detail: The vendor's System Requirements page (last updated 29 September 2026) states that the mobile app runs on Android 7.0 or above with a minimum of 4GB RAM, and on iOS 15.0 or above for Apple devices. No storage figure is published. An older FAQ page on joblogic.com still quotes Android 4.0 upwards; the System Requirements page is the current figure and matches the Google Play listing.

requirements.requirement: Android app from Google Play, for phones and tablets
requirements.detail: The Android app is published on Google Play as Joblogic (package com.tracer.joblogic, developer JobLogic Limited). When checked on 15 October 2026 the listing showed version 1.186.2, updated 5 October 2026, with a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0), and device chips for Phone and Tablet. The vendor's user guide tells Android users to download the app from Google Play.

requirements.requirement: Offline working, with a connection needed to receive new visits
requirements.detail: The vendor's FAQ says Joblogic Mobile can be used without signal when installed from Google Play or the App Store, and that once offline working is enabled engineers can log jobs and quotes offline. It also says an internet connection is required to download new visit details to the device in the first place, and that jobs can take up to 10 minutes to arrive on a device using the offline version. The user guide adds a manual sync option under Status. The vendor does not publish how much data is cached on the device.

requirements.requirement: Asset scanning by QR code or barcode, through the camera
requirements.detail: The user guide says the Scan option can be used to search for Joblogic assets by QR code or barcode, and that it opens the device camera. Codes that are not already set up against an asset in Joblogic return no result. No support for a dedicated hardware scan engine or an external scanner is documented, so on any device the scan path is the camera.

requirements.requirement: Photos, attachments and customer signatures in the app
requirements.detail: The user guide documents an attachments area where engineers add photos and files or take a photo with the camera, including several images at once, and receipt photos on expenses. At completion the customer can be asked to sign, and the engineer can sign too; depending on back office settings a signature may be mandatory. Job forms appear once the engineer marks themselves On Site, and a partly completed form is saved only up to the last finished page.

requirements.requirement: GPS tracking module and device settings for background running
requirements.detail: The vendor's job tracking page says workers can be monitored from the office through a GPS tracking module. The user guide's first run prompts cover Low Power Mode, letting the app run in the background, an overlay setting and biometric login, and its View On Map route works only with signal and a correctly set up address. No GNSS accuracy or location hardware requirement is published.

requirements.requirement: Windows: no Windows mobile app, web product in a browser
requirements.detail: The System Requirements page states that Joblogic is not available on Windows phones, and no native Windows app is published. The web product is described as working across all modern browsers as long as they support HTML 5, with a recommendation to accept browser updates. No specific browser list or version numbers are published.

recommended.why: Joblogic's engineer features (forms, certificates, photos, signatures, camera asset scanning and offline working) live in the Android app, so the device an engineer carries needs to run that app well rather than a browser. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 against a published requirement of Android 7.0 or later, and carries 8GB of RAM against a published minimum of 4GB, so it clears the RAM figure with room to spare rather than sitting on it. The forms Joblogic describes (risk assessments, gas and electrical certificates, service sheets) run to several pages, and the 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen shows more of each page at once than the 8 or 6 inch options, which also helps when a customer signs on screen. The IP68 and MIL-STD-810H ratings cover rain on a roof, dust in a plant room and drops from a ladder, and the 13MP rear camera with flash is the scan and photo path the app documents. It fits both the charging dock and the vehicle mounting dock.

recommended.why: The Tuga A8 is the closer call. It runs the same Joblogic Android app on an 8 inch screen that is big enough for job forms without the size of the A10, and small enough to hold in one hand up a ladder. It runs Android 12 with Google Play, above the Android 7.0 requirement, and its 6GB of RAM is above Joblogic's 4GB minimum, though below the A10's 8GB. Its 1000 nit screen suits engineers who spend much of the day outside, the 8000mAh battery is removable for long days, and VESA mount points and a pogo pin connector suit a van fit. Against the A10 it is sealed to IP67 rather than IP68, has no MIL-STD rating, a lower 1280 x 800 resolution, and does not fit the charging dock. At £379 it costs £70 less than the A10.

recommended.why: For engineers who want something that goes in a pocket or a belt holster at 277g, the Tuga A6 runs the same Joblogic Android app on a 6 inch handheld, and the Google Play listing carries a Phone device chip, so a phone-sized layout is one the vendor publishes for. It runs Android 15, well above the Android 7.0 requirement, but be clear on memory: its 4GB of RAM meets Joblogic's 4GB minimum exactly, with no headroom, so for heavy daily form filling the A10 or A8 is the safer choice and a trial unit is worth running first. It has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but Joblogic documents camera scanning only, so plan on the 13MP rear camera. The trade-off is screen area: a 6 inch display shows less of a long certificate or a signature box than the larger tablets.

recommended.why: Joblogic has no Windows app and says it is not available on Windows phones. The Tuga W10 runs Windows 11 Pro, so it can run the Joblogic web product in a current desktop browser, which the vendor says works in any modern HTML 5 browser. That makes it a fit for a scheduler's desk, a site office or a workshop counter, and it has Ethernet and HDMI for a fixed position. It is not the device for an engineer: the camera asset scanning, offline working, photos and signatures the vendor documents are in the mobile app, which does not run on Windows, and the W10 is IP65 rather than IP68, so it is protected against water jets but not rated for immersion.

setup_steps: Ask your Joblogic administrator to set the engineer up as a mobile user in your Joblogic account and to enable offline working if your team needs it.
On the Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install Joblogic (package com.tracer.joblogic, developer JobLogic Limited), then sign in with the engineer's details.

Work through the first run prompts the user guide describes: Low Power Mode, letting the app run in the background, the overlay setting and biometric login. Allow camera and location access so the Scan option and the GPS tracking module can work.

Before the first job without signal, keep the device online long enough to download the engineer's visit details. The vendor says new jobs can take up to 10 minutes to arrive on a device using the offline version, and the Status screen has a manual sync option.
Test the Scan option against an asset whose QR code or barcode is already set up in Joblogic, and complete a test job with photos and a signature, before rolling out to the team.
On a Tuga W10, open the Joblogic web product in Edge or Chrome and keep the browser updated, as the vendor recommends. Use it for office work; it will not run the mobile app.

For the A10 and A8, fit the vehicle mounting dock in the van; for the A10 and W10, add the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6, add the belt holster. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out.

faq.q: Will Joblogic run on the Tuga A10?
faq.a: Joblogic publishes a requirement of Android 7.0 or above with a minimum of 4GB RAM, and its Google Play listing gives a minimum API level of 24 (Android 7.0). The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with Google Play and has 8GB RAM and 128GB storage, so it meets each published figure. The Tuga A8 (Android 12, 6GB RAM) also meets them, and the Tuga A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM) meets them with no RAM headroom. We do not describe any device as certified or tested by Joblogic; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications.

faq.q: Does Joblogic work without signal on these tablets?
faq.a: The vendor's FAQ says Joblogic Mobile can be used without signal when installed from Google Play, and that with offline working enabled engineers can log jobs and quotes offline. A connection is needed to download new visit details in the first place, and the vendor says jobs can take up to 10 minutes to arrive on a device using the offline version. The A10, A8 and A6 all run the Google Play app. A Tuga W10 can only use the web product in a browser, and the vendor does not document offline working there.

faq.q: Can engineers scan asset QR codes and barcodes, and does the A6's scanner help?
faq.a: Joblogic's user guide documents a Scan option that opens the camera to find assets by QR code or barcode, provided the code is already set up in Joblogic. The A10, A8 and A6 all have a 13MP rear camera with flash, and on each of them scanning runs through the camera via the app. The A6 also has a Zebra 2D scan engine, but the vendor documents no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support, so do not buy it for that reason alone.

faq.q: Should engineers have the 10.1 inch A10 or the 8 inch A8?
faq.a: Both meet Joblogic's published requirements. The A10 has more RAM (8GB against 6GB), a sharper 1920 x 1200 screen for multi-page forms and certificates, IP68 against IP67, and MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not have. The A8 has a 1000 nit screen against the A10's 350 nits, a removable battery, VESA mount points, and costs £379 against £449. Engineers who mostly work outdoors or do long days away from a charger may prefer the A8; those filling in long forms or working in wetter, harder conditions are better served by the A10.

faq.q: Can we trial one unit first, and do you invoice businesses?
faq.a: Yes to both. A single trial unit before a fleet order is welcome. Business buyers can request a quote and pay by bank transfer on a proforma invoice. Tuga Hardware is the trading name of Destello Tech Ltd and is not VAT registered, so there is no VAT to add to the £449 (A10), £379 (A8), £349 (A6) or £649 (W10) prices. Delivery is free worldwide in 7 to 10 working days, with 30-day returns and a 12-month warranty. Multi-unit discounts apply automatically: 3% at 2 units, 5% at 3 to 4, 8% at 5 to 9 and 10% at 10 or more.

not_recommended_note: Joblogic has no Windows app and says it is not available on Windows phones, so the Tuga W10 only runs the web product in a browser. The engineer features the vendor documents (camera asset scanning, offline working, photos, signatures and job forms) are in the mobile app, so a W10 suits an office or workshop desk, not an engineer on site. On the Android side, the only scan method the vendor documents is the camera, with no dedicated scan engine or external scanner support published, so the A6's Zebra 2D scan engine is not a documented Joblogic input. The Tuga A6's 4GB of RAM meets the published 4GB minimum exactly, with no margin. The vendor publishes no storage figure, no screen-size guidance and no NFC or RFID support, so the NFC radio on the A10, A8 and A6 should not be treated as a Joblogic feature. The vendor's GPS tracking module is described from the office side only; it does not publish what location accuracy it needs from a device.
